Interface Shader

All Known Implementing Classes:
DissolveShader, ExpandShader, FadeShader, PaintShader, ParallelEffect, SequentialEffect, SlideShader, StretchShader, SweepShader
public interface Shader
Interface representing a shader that applies visual effects to terminal cells.

The Shader interface is the core abstraction for all visual effects. It defines the contract for objects that can transform terminal cell appearance over time.

Design Philosophy:

  • Separation of Timing and Rendering: The default process(TFxDuration, Buffer, Rect) method handles timer updates, while execute(TFxDuration, Rect, Buffer) handles the actual rendering logic.
  • Flexible Configuration: Shaders can be configured with filters, patterns, color spaces, and areas through optional methods.
  • Composability: Shaders can be copied and combined to create complex effects.

Implementation Pattern:

Most shader implementations should:

  1. Store an EffectTimer for timing control
  2. Implement execute(TFxDuration, Rect, Buffer) to perform the actual cell transformations
  3. Implement done() to check if the effect is complete
  4. Implement copy() to support effect composition

The default process(TFxDuration, Buffer, Rect) implementation handles timer updates automatically, so you typically only need to override execute(TFxDuration, Rect, Buffer). Only override process(TFxDuration, Buffer, Rect) if you need custom timer handling (e.g., for effects that don't use timers).

Example Implementation: 

public class MyShader implements Shader {
    private final EffectTimer timer;
    private final Color targetColor;
    
    public MyShader(Color targetColor, EffectTimer timer) {
        this.targetColor = targetColor;
        this.timer = timer;
    }
    
    {@literal @}Override
    public String name() { return "my-effect"; }
    
    {@literal @}Override
    public EffectTimer timer() { return timer; }
    
    {@literal @}Override
    public boolean done() { return timer.done(); }
    
    {@literal @}Override
    public void execute(TFxDuration duration, Rect area, Buffer buffer) {
        float alpha = timer.alpha();
        // Apply effect based on alpha...
    }
    
    {@literal @}Override
    public Shader copy() {
        return new MyShader(targetColor, timer);
    }
}

  • Method Details

    • name

      String name()
      Returns the name of this shader.
      Returns:
      the shader name

    • process

      default TFxDuration process(TFxDuration duration, Buffer buffer, Rect area)
      Processes the shader for the given duration.

      The default implementation: 1. Updates the timer with the given duration (if a timer exists) 2. Calls execute(TFxDuration, Rect, Buffer) with the current state 3. Returns any overflow duration

      Most effects should use this default implementation and implement execute(TFxDuration, Rect, Buffer) instead. Only override this if you need custom timer handling.

      Parameters:
      duration - The duration to process the shader for
      buffer - The buffer where the shader will be applied
      area - The rectangular area within the buffer where the shader will be applied
      Returns:
      The overflow duration if the shader is done, or null if still running

    • execute

      default void execute(TFxDuration duration, Rect area, Buffer buffer)
      Executes the shader effect after the duration has been applied to the timer.

      This is the main implementation point for most effects, and is called by the default process(TFxDuration, Buffer, Rect) implementation.

      Parameters:
      duration - The duration to process the shader for
      area - The rectangular area within the buffer where the shader will be applied
      buffer - The buffer where the shader will be applied

    • reverse

      default void reverse()
      Reverses the shader's playback direction.

      This method reverses the timer direction, causing the effect to play backwards. The default implementation reverses the timer if one exists.

    • setLoopMode

      default void setLoopMode(LoopMode mode)
      Sets the loop mode for this shader's timer.

      This method sets the loop mode on the underlying timer, controlling what happens when the effect reaches its end. See LoopMode for available modes.

      Parameters:
      mode - the loop mode to set
